title: Protocol for using autoclaved intertidal sediment as a medium to enrich marine cable bacteria
protocol: Sieve the stored sediment through a 0.5 mm mesh screen.
Remove large fauna, rocks, and debris from the sieved sediment.
Homogenize the sieved sediment by physical mixing.
Introduce nitrogen gas into the homogenized sediment to reduce oxygen exposure.
Fill 100 mL autoclave-safe glass bottles with homogenized sediment to about ¾ of their volume.
Fill 1000 mL autoclave-safe bottles with seawater to about ¾ of their volume.
Autoclave the glass bottles at 120°C for 1–2 hours.
Allow the autoclaved sediment and seawater to cool down to about 25°C before use.
Store sealed containers containing cooled autoclaved sediment at approximately 25°C until inoculation.
Place the extracted plugs of sediment in a glass Petri dish.
Add seawater or artificial seawater to the Petri dish.
Gently shake the Petri dish to allow the sediment particles to separate from the CB filaments.
Remove sediment-laden water from the Petri dish.
Repeat shaking and removal until the filamentous structure of CB can be observed.
Use a fabricated glass hook to pick CB filaments from the remainder of the washed sediment plug(s).
Push the hook gently into a suboxic zone of the remaining washed sample, identified by its grayish color.
Swirl the hook gently several times (3–7).
Slowly pull the hook away from the sample and look for filamentous structures of CB connecting to the sediment.
Collect the filaments by pulling the hook apart from the sediment.
Transfer the isolated CB filaments to a droplet of washing solution on a microscopic slide.
Use a clean glass needle to scrape the biomass off the glass hook.
Resuspend the biomass in the droplet of washing solution.
Repeat steps until the biomass appears free of sediment particles.
Pick up the washed biomass with another clean glass needle.
Transfer the washed biomass into the surface layer of the autoclaved sediment.
Submerge the inoculated sediment slowly into an aerated aquarium filled with autoclaved medium.
Culture the inoculated sediment.
Evaluate the growth and presence of cable bacteria by measuring vertical chemical profiles of oxygen, sulfide, and pH using microelectrodes.
